title: Demo tenant seed data spec (org/projects/routes/prompt sets) — working
content:
Purpose / why this doc exists
We need the demo tenant to look “already in use” the moment an AE/SE logs in: projects exist, routes are configured, API keys are present, dashboards have realistic charts (cost/latency/errors), and the story-specific artifacts (prompt sets, eval runs, rollouts) are ready.

This is a working seed-data spec that the bootstrap + reset automation should implement. It is intentionally opinionated (naming, default dashboards, distributions) to reduce demo variance.

Scope
In scope
- Seeded org + projects + members (RBAC)
- Seeded model routes (pinned versions + controlled fallback)
- Seeded prompt sets + eval runs (for “Optimize / regression prevention” story)
- Seeded synthetic usage + traces + errors to populate Console views
- Naming conventions that support parallel demos without cross-demo contamination

Out of scope (for seed)
- Real customer data, real documents, or anything that resembles a customer identifier
- Any irreversible billing / invoice generation (we use billing sandbox)
- “Perfect realism” in every chart; goal is believable + stable + explainable

Owner / operational assumptions
- SEs can run a single bootstrap/reset command (see ENG-4862) and get to green within minutes.
- Synthetic traffic generator runs on a schedule (or can be triggered) to keep “last 1h / last 24h” charts non-empty.
- Models used in demo are pinned and changes are controlled (see ENG-4840 + ADR).


1) Org + access model
Org name (fixed)
- Redwood Demo (Internal)

Org slug (fixed)
- redwood-demo

RBAC groups (seeded)
- Demo Admins: full org admin (limited membership)
- Demo SEs: project admin on demo projects + read-only on org settings
- Demo AEs: project member (can view keys/usage for their scoped demo project only)
- Security Review Readonly: read-only role scoped to the “enterprise-security” project (screenshare-safe)

Seeded members (internal only; add via automation)
- Markus Klein (Demo Admins)
- Simran Kaur (Demo Admins)
- Talia Benson (Demo Admins)
- Allison Grant (Demo SEs)
- Renee Sullivan (Demo SEs)
- (Optional) Avery Johnson / Priyom Das / Hannah Schmitt (Demo AEs) for pilot

Notes
- Keep “Demo AEs” permissions deliberately narrow. AEs should not see org-wide admin knobs during a live call.
- Do not seed external emails. Partner access is separate and must be time-bound.


2) Project taxonomy + naming conventions
We need two things simultaneously:
(1) Stable “canonical” projects that screenshots and enablement materials reference.
(2) A mechanism for parallel demos that isolates traffic + keys + dashboards per session.

2.1 Canonical (always present) projects
A) Project: demo-core-api
- Purpose: live API demo (streaming, structured output, tool calling, retries)
- Default time range during demo: last 15m / last 1h (needs ongoing synthetic traffic)

B) Project: demo-economics
- Purpose: batching/caching toggles; token-level cost breakdown; A/B comparison
- Requirement: contains both a “baseline” route and an “optimized” route with visibly different cost/latency characteristics

C) Project: demo-reliability
- Purpose: fallback routing, region/model variant failover, graceful degradation
- Requirement: includes one route with a safe fallback policy and seeded “incident-like” spike in errors for historical charts

D) Project: demo-observability
- Purpose: traces, error analysis, rollout view, canary/A-B
- Requirement: contains at least two deployments/versions or route revisions to show “before/after”

E) Project: demo-enterprise-security
- Purpose: narrative/screenshots only; safe to show settings pages (SSO/SAML, audit log view, retention controls)
- Requirement: zero live API keys displayed by default; minimize risk of “clicking into secrets”

2.2 Parallel demo session projects (ephemeral)
Create a new project per live customer demo when we need strict isolation.

Project naming format
- demo-session-<yyyy-mm-dd>-<slot>-<ae-initials>-<region>
Examples
- demo-session-2026-02-14-1-aj-us
- demo-session-2026-02-14-2-hs-eu

Slot guidance
- 1..6 (simple integer). If more are needed, create additional org “namespaces” only as a last resort.

Ephemeral project lifecycle
- Created automatically by bootstrap when “--session” flag is used.
- Deleted or reset back to template after demo (within 24h).
- Must have its own API keys and traffic generator labels.


3) Models + version pinning (demo-safe)
We seed a small number of “demo routes” per project that map to pinned model versions. Exact internal IDs may differ per region; the key is that the names are stable for GTM and the pinned references are stable for Eng.

3.1 Canonical model labels (what GTM sees)
- Redwood Chat XL
- Redwood Chat M
- Redwood Embeddings
- Redwood Rerank

3.2 Pinned catalog references (what the system uses)
(Example placeholders; final IDs come from the model catalog)
- rw.chat-xl: llama-3.1-70b-instruct@2025-10-15
- rw.chat-m: llama-3.1-8b-instruct@2025-10-15
- rw.embed: bge-m3@2025-09-30
- rw.rerank: bge-reranker-v2-m3@2025-09-30

3.3 Regions
Seed configuration should support at least:
- us-east (default)
- eu-west (for EMEA variant)

3.4 Fallback policy (demo-safe)
Goal: if capacity is constrained or a region has issues, demo still works and the story remains credible.

Rules
- Only fallback within the same “family” label (Chat XL -> Chat M) unless explicitly in the reliability demo.
- Fallback order (normal demos):
  1) same model, different region (if allowed by prospect’s residency constraints)
  2) compatible smaller model in same region

Reliability demo route intentionally shows:
- Primary: Chat XL in us-east
- Fallback: Chat M in us-east, then Chat M in eu-west (configurable)


4) Routes per project (seeded)
All routes should be created with stable route names and short descriptions visible in Console.

4.1 demo-core-api routes
- /demo/chat-stream
  - Model: Redwood Chat XL
  - Features enabled: streaming ON, tool calling ON, structured output ON
  - Rate limit: conservative but not demo-breaking (avoid 429 under normal use)

- /demo/chat-structured
  - Model: Redwood Chat M
  - Features enabled: structured output ON
  - Used for “JSON you can trust” moment

- /demo/tools
  - Model: Redwood Chat XL
  - Tools: “get_weather”, “lookup_order_status” (fake) with deterministic stub responses
  - Important: tool call outputs must be stable across runs (avoid model drift)

4.2 demo-economics routes
- /demo/econ/baseline
  - Model: Redwood Chat M
  - Batching: OFF (or minimal)
  - Prefix/KV cache: OFF
  - Goal: higher cost per 1k tokens; lower throughput

- /demo/econ/optimized
  - Model: Redwood Chat M (same model to keep comparison clean)
  - Batching: ON (workload-aware)
  - Prefix/KV cache: ON (with seeded repeated prefixes)
  - Goal: visible reduction in cost per 1k tokens with acceptable latency change

- /demo/econ/embeddings
  - Model: Redwood Embeddings
  - Used to show non-chat workloads and cost breakdown by endpoint

4.3 demo-reliability routes
- /demo/reliable/chat
  - Model: Redwood Chat XL
  - Fallback: enabled (per policy above)
  - Retry policy: enabled (client + server hints)

- /demo/reliable/failover-sim
  - Same as above but with a “failure injection” toggle (only for synthetic traffic generator)
  - Used to generate historical error spike without risking live call steps

4.4 demo-observability routes
- /demo/obs/chat
  - Model: Redwood Chat M
  - Tracing: ON (include request_id / trace_id)

- /demo/obs/canary
  - Two revisions: revA (baseline prompts), revB (slightly different system prompt)
  - Traffic split: 90/10
  - Used to show rollout view + comparison in latency/error

4.5 demo-enterprise-security routes
- None by default.
- If needed for internal dry runs, create /internal/security-smoke but hide from default project views and ensure keys are not visible to AEs.


5) API keys (seeded) + scoping
We seed keys primarily so the demo app and traffic generator work out of the box. Keys must be least-privilege and rotateable.

Key types
A) demo-traffic-generator (service key)
- Scope: can call seeded routes in all demo projects; can write trace headers
- Stored: internal secrets manager (not visible in Console to non-admin)

B) demo-se-live (SE key)
- Scope: call routes + view usage for canonical projects
- Rotation: monthly or after incident

C) demo-ae-session (per-session key)
- Scope: only the session project (demo-session-...)
- TTL: short-lived (target <= 7 days)
- Created at session bootstrap; revoked at reset

Console display rules
- Default Console view should not show full secrets. Use last-4 + created timestamp.


6) Prompt sets + evals (seeded)
We seed prompt sets to support:
- A “known-good outputs” story (repeatability)
- A “regression alert” story (if a new model/version changes behavior)

Prompt set naming
- ps-demo-customer-support-triage
- ps-demo-json-extraction
- ps-demo-tool-calling

Each prompt set should include
- 10–25 prompts (enough for charts, not huge)
- Tags: “demo”, plus the scenario tag (economics, reliability, etc.)
- Stored expected outputs for 3–5 prompts only (to avoid overfitting and maintenance)

Seeded eval runs
- eval-demo-baseline (against Chat M pinned)
- eval-demo-canary (against Chat XL pinned)

Evaluation metrics (simple + explainable)
- JSON validity rate (for structured output prompts)
- Tool-call correctness rate (did it call the tool when appropriate)
- Qualitative score stub (0–5) for a handful of prompts

Important constraints
- All prompts must be obviously synthetic (no names, no real tickets, no “actual orders”).
- Avoid prompts that create policy risk in a live demo (e.g., medical or legal advice). Keep it enterprise-safe.


7) Synthetic usage + dashboard realism requirements
The Console must show believable charts for:
- Requests, tokens in/out
- Latency p50/p95
- Error rate (with at least some non-zero errors in last 7d)
- Cost breakdown by route/model
- Caching/batching impact (in demo-economics)
- Traces for a handful of recent requests

7.1 Traffic generator distribution (target)
We seed ongoing traffic with stable distributions so charts look “alive” without being chaotic.

Global cadence
- Every 2 minutes: small burst for each canonical project
- Every hour: larger burst to create visible hourly bars
- Every day (off-hours): a controlled “error spike” in demo-reliability to create historical incident visuals

Per-project request mix (approx)
- demo-core-api: 60% /demo/chat-stream, 25% /demo/chat-structured, 15% /demo/tools
- demo-economics: 40% /econ/baseline, 40% /econ/optimized, 20% /econ/embeddings
- demo-reliability: 80% /reliable/chat, 20% /reliable/failover-sim
- demo-observability: 70% /obs/chat, 30% /obs/canary

Latency targets (believable, not “too perfect”)
- Chat XL: p50 700–1200ms, p95 1800–3000ms (streaming starts faster)
- Chat M: p50 300–700ms, p95 900–1600ms
- Embeddings: p50 80–200ms, p95 250–500ms

Error injection (bounded)
- Normal hours: ~0.2% 5xx on demo-reliability failover-sim only
- Daily “spike” window: 3–8 minutes at 3–5% 5xx to show error analysis + fallback (must not break live routes)
- Occasional 429s: do NOT inject by default; this has bitten us in real demos (see SUP-4127). Only enable in internal stress tests.

Token shapes (so cost charts look real)
- Mix of short and medium prompts. Target output tokens:
  - 50%: 100–250 output tokens
  - 35%: 250–600 output tokens
  - 15%: 600–1200 output tokens
- Ensure repeated prefixes for caching demo (same system prompt across bursts).

7.2 Traces
- Ensure at least 10 traceable requests exist in last 15 minutes for demo-observability.
- Add stable attributes: route_name, model_label, region, project, request_source (traffic-generator vs live-demo-app).

7.3 Time ranges / empty state protection
Seed data must ensure “Last 1h” and “Last 24h” views show activity.
- If generator is paused, the healthcheck should instruct to run it before the demo.


8) Seeded “story beats” (what the SE can reliably point at)
We should be able to confidently say:
- “Here’s the core route” (core-api) with a recent streaming request visible in traces.
- “Here’s the cost/latency breakdown” (economics) showing baseline vs optimized with different cost per 1k tokens.
- “Here’s a past reliability event” (reliability) with an error spike and fallback recovery.
- “Here’s a rollout” (observability) with canary split and a small difference in metric.
- “Here are audit logs / retention controls” (enterprise-security) without exposing secrets.

Seeded annotations / descriptions (helpful in Console)
- Each route description should be written like a human note, not an internal ID.
  Example: “Optimized route (batching+cache enabled) for cost/latency tradeoff demo.”


9) Reset behavior expectations (for automation)
After reset, the following must be true within 5 minutes:
- Canonical projects exist with routes + descriptions intact
- Any demo-session projects from prior day are removed (or archived) unless flagged “keep”
- Keys are rotated as configured
- Synthetic traffic generator is running (or last run < 10 minutes ago)
- Healthcheck returns green (quota, model availability, ingestion)

What reset should NOT do
- It should not change the canonical route names (these are referenced in enablement materials).
- It should not swap the demo model pins silently.


10) Validation checklist (quick manual sanity)
SE can run this in 2–3 minutes before a call:
- Login -> Redwood Demo (Internal) loads and shows projects immediately
- demo-core-api: Requests graph non-zero in last 15m
- demo-economics: cost breakdown shows both /baseline and /optimized in the legend
- demo-reliability: error analysis shows at least some events in last 7d (not necessarily last hour)
- demo-observability: traces show at least 3 recent requests with trace_id
- demo-enterprise-security: audit log page loads; no secrets visible by default


Open questions / TODOs
- Confirm final catalog IDs + pin dates for Chat XL/Chat M in us-east and eu-west (needs Eng + model onboarding). We should maintain a single “demo-models.yaml/json” source of truth.
- Decide whether demo-observability canary should show a small *quality* difference (not just latency). If yes, how do we measure without demo risk?
- EMEA variant: do we maintain separate canonical projects (demo-*-eu) or just switch region in routes? Current preference: switchable route policy; keep one set of project names.
- Confirm default Console landing page + saved views to minimize clicking during live call (Design/Console).

Change log (manual)
- 2025-11-04: initial working draft from kickoff.
- 2025-12-03: added session project naming + EMEA notes.
- 2026-01-23: tightened error injection (avoid 429) after field incidents; added enterprise-security “no keys visible” requirement.
- 2026-02-14: aligned route set to include structured output + tool calling explicitly; updated validation checklist for traces.
